name: Cholinergic
vitals: Bradycardia, bronchorrhea, bronchospasm; may be tachycardic from nicotinic effect
mental: Anxious then depressed; seizures; fasciculations and weakness
tell: The patient is wet and cannot ventilate. Secretions, not pupils, are the finding that matters.

name: Anticholinergic
onset: 30 min to hours; may persist days
vitals: Tachycardia, hyperthermia, urinary retention, absent bowel sounds
mental: Agitated delirium, mumbling speech, picking at air, no orientation
tell: Dry skin and dry axillae. This is the single finding that separates it from a sympathomimetic.

name: Sympathomimetic
tell: Looks like anticholinergic but the patient is soaking wet and has bowel sounds. Sweat is the discriminator.

name: Opioid
pupils: Miosis (may be normal with meperidine, tramadol, or mixed ingestion)
vitals: Hypoventilation — the defining sign — then bradycardia and hypotension
tell: Respiratory rate and tidal volume, not pupils. A normal pupil does not exclude it.

name: Sedative-hypnotic
vitals: Near-normal early; hypoventilation and hypotension when deep
mental: Sedation to coma with preserved respiratory drive until late
tell: Sedation without any autonomic signature. If the vitals are unremarkable, think here.

name: Serotonin syndrome
onset: Hours — often within 24 h of a dose change
mental: Agitation; clonus and hyperreflexia, greater in the legs than the arms; ocular clonus
tell: Clonus. Rapid onset plus lower-limb-dominant hyperreflexia separates it from neuroleptic malignant syndrome, which builds over days with lead-pipe rigidity and hyporeflexia.

name: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome
onset: Days to weeks after starting or increasing an antipsychotic
vitals: Hyperthermia, autonomic instability, raised creatine kinase
mental: Stupor and mutism; generalised lead-pipe rigidity with hyporeflexia
tell: Slow onset and lead-pipe rigidity without clonus. Also consider abrupt withdrawal of levodopa or a dopamine agonist, which produces an identical picture.
agents: Withdrawal of levodopa or a dopamine agonist

name: Metabolic acidosis with hyperventilation
vitals: Tachypnoea with a wide anion gap; hyperthermia in uncoupler poisoning
mental: Tinnitus and agitation early, then confusion and coma
tell: A patient breathing hard with a wide anion gap and no obvious cause. This is the pattern that gets attributed to sepsis or anxiety until the gas comes back.
